worked_examples.input_result: Taken together, the polarization data and the immersion data provide two independent lines of evidence that converge on the same ranking: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd degrades far faster than 317L SS. Neither observation alone rules out that the apparent difference is an artifact of one particular test method; the pair together shows the faster degradation of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd holds across two different measurement approaches (electrochemical and immersion), which is stronger support for a real, method-independent material difference than either measurement gives on its own.

Does not establish the mechanism responsible for the faster degradation

worked_examples.question: What does this measurement, read together with the established earlier result below, settle about STR/chemistry/bonding that neither settles on its own? Say what the combination supports and what it leaves open.
worked_examples.input_result: FTIR (GATR) assigns specific vibrational bands to bond types present in the PPAm film -- N-H (3350/3210 cm-1), aliphatic C-H, -N=C=O/-C=N (2245/2180 cm-1), C=O/C=N (1645 cm-1), C-N (1230 cm-1) -- while ToF-SIMS independently detects N-containing fragment ions (CH4N m/z 30, C3H9N m/z 59, C4H10N m/z 72) among the CxHy ion set at the surface. Put together, the two techniques give converging, independent confirmation that nitrogen is retained as part of the film's molecular structure and is detectable both as vibrational bonding signatures and as surface mass fragments -- a stronger basis for asserting N retention than either technique alone, since FTIR could in principle reflect subsurface/bulk species and SIMS fragment masses alone do not confirm a bonding assignment.
input_limits: ToF-SIMS fragment formulas (CH4N, C3H9N, C4H10N) are mass-only identifications and cannot by themselves specify which functional group (amine N-H vs nitrile/isocyanate vs C=O/C=N) the nitrogen belongs to, so they cannot confirm the specific bond assignments FTIR makes

the FTIR bands attributed to plasma-fragmentation products (-N=C=O/-C=N at 2245/2180 cm-1, C=O/C=N at 1645 cm-1) have no corresponding fragment explicitly identified in the cited SIMS ion list, so the pairing does not show that SIMS detects those specific new groups
worked_examples.new_obs: Starred NO vibration, N=N, N-N and N-O stretch bands appear in NO-PPAm and are absent from the PPAm spectrum
worked_examples.proposition: Because A already establishes (via converging FTIR bond assignments and ToF-SIMS fragment ions) that the PPAm film retains nitrogen within its own molecular structure (e.g., amine N-H, C-N, and other N-containing groups), the new starred NO-vibration, N=N, N-N, and N-O stretch bands that B shows appearing in NO-PPAm but absent from plain PPAm support that these new bands arise from NO becoming chemically incorporated onto the pre-existing, structurally-retained nitrogen framework of the film, rather than reflecting unrelated new chemistry or merely physisorbed, unreacted NO gas sitting on an otherwise inert surface.
limits: the combination does not indicate which of the several nitrogen-containing groups already identified in A (amine N-H, C-N backbone, or the plasma-fragmentation-derived C=N/isocyanate nitrogen) is the actual site where NO attaches to produce the new bands in B, since B's spectral comparison does not map the new bands onto a specific precursor group
